items.note: Association named, organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery built 1891 - all present in narrative 1.
Article VII quoted verbatim: paid by pounds of butterfat ascertained by test, not by weight of milk, and the test of the station where he delivers governs.
States the rule is what made a wrong test cost money (Falke: under payment by weight nothing that follows would have cost any man a dollar; Effie's 'hinge').

Effie Loomis secretary and Hobart Sill buttermaker in narrative 1; Wilbur Teague and his ledger line ruled from 1905 in narrative 2 - all three officers named with roles inside this batch's Section A.
Selby Vose appears nowhere in the three Section A narratives. His parentage and 1913 managership are given only at B3, and credit never travels from B-G into Section A.
Narrative 2 gives the 1898 station account with the 'station gain, 3,040 lb, five and a quarter per cent, as usual' line and notes the loss was already in the ledgers under a name.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green.

List-type item with no REQUIRED line; core workflow present in narrative 2 (milk weighed, sampled, tested, separated; cream down daily to Larrow Green, skim back), with the 17.6 c.c. pipette charge and '8 per cent neck' test bottles quoted inside Section A. 'Composite' sample and the read-on-the-neck mechanism are not spelled out, but the core fact is stated.
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice of 14 April 1897; in use from 1 May 1897, with the 1898 and 1899 rivals rejected.
Full invoice itemized: 6 doz. pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 doz. bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, total $77.93.
States the shortfall was flat - 0.19 short of the truth, 'the same in February as in July' - and argues five hundredths in winter cannot carry nineteen hundredths in July.

States the pipette is the one instrument the plant cannot check against anything else and that from inside nobody could see it. The burette and its absence in the county are not named in Section A, but the item's claim is asserted.
Name and birth year only. Section A never gives the twenty-nine seasons / 1896-1924 service span nor the dismissal of 30 April 1925; both bolded elements missing.

The test book is named and quoted, but that is the element shared with A3.3 and A3.4, both of which are credited. A3.2's own aspect - the bench routine, the book's columns (date, patron, pounds, test, fat), one hand for twenty-nine seasons, corrections crossed and initialed - is absent. Key's no-double-scoring rule: a solver stating nothing but the shared element takes one item, not the others.
Both required figures: 1896 average 3.80 on Sill's borrowed glass, 3.61 from 1898 and within three hundredths of it every year, with the step located at the change of glassware.
Pipette broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure nine weeks to 10 July, tests at 3.80, return to 3.61 with the question mark quoted; the six-week corruption explicitly rejected.
Narrative 1: Keddie married Orra Brant, Emmet Brant's sister - 'the tie that later put the tester at the biggest patron's table.'
No 1919 water circular and no Keddie statement of 17 March 1925 anywhere in Section A. The circular appears only at B3, from which credit cannot travel.
Keddie's 1934 death, the impounding of the test book and its 1959 deposit are not stated in Section A.
Granddaughter, with the full derivation through Duncan and the birth-year arithmetic; the great-niece printings identified as press-release error and retraction.

Second cousins with a correct derivation (+1). Abstention half (A08): the full-vs-half sibling question is listed under 'what the sources leave open' - a correct abstention, so no gullibility deduction - but the run says that if Hazel is right the two women are 'half second cousins', instead of the required statement that it does not change the answer. Second bolded element unmet: 0.

Gideon Vose, his father, with the nephew story defeated; significance given - the Voses wrote Article VII and then ran the office enforcing it against a fault in the instrument that rule made decisive, plus the Vose Jerseys at 4.56.

Correct abstention on A01: 'nothing could settle it', 'Verdict: not proven'. The lean to 'probably nonexistent' sits inside a sentence carrying the declining qualifier, so under the key's operational test it is an abstention, not an assertion - no -2. Second point earned: hearsay claimants on one side, a flat family denial on the other, no marriage, document or birth record either way, and the pre-1889 diary pages not preserved.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95; 95 percent of true, short 5 percent, one part in twenty. 16.27 identified and rejected.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19 of a point; 3.16, 0.17 and 0.21 all correctly set aside.
40,000,000 lb over the 25 full years 1898-1922; 1,520,000 - 1,444,000 = 76,000 lb, cross-checked against the station-gain entries. 44,000,000 rejected.
76,000 x $0.25 = $19,000; award $3,800 = 0.20, one fifth. Both money and fraction given; 27 cents, $19,600 and $3,500 rejected.
3.42 / 0.95 = 3.60; 7,200 lb true; 360 lb owed, with two independent checks.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the 1910 price sourced and the $90.00 alternative correctly explained as the period average.
